reviewed_properties: Componentwise no-follow directory descriptors and identity checks precede root fstatvfs. Data files are only statted; content reads are limited to bounded fixed mountinfo.

CLI fixed /data requires a unique exact containing mount with matching device. Imported fixture API defaults require_exact_mount=False and reports that choice; it still requires a unique device-matching containing mount.
Mount snapshot excludes listed nested mounts including same-device paths, and traversal excludes cross-device entries.

Entry, directory, depth, error, shared output-row, mountinfo-byte and cooperative elapsed budgets bound work. Inode dedup memory is bounded by entry count; output is row bounded rather than a separate fixed serialized-byte cap.
Only mount ID, parent ID, device, mountpoint and identity checks are exported; mount source/options are omitted.
Aggregate wording now correctly states observed sums, not a certified lower bound on current disk use.
limits: Mountinfo is a bounded observation with no mount-namespace lock. Concurrent same-device mount additions or root/ancestor replacement after checks may evade the snapshot boundaries; this helper does not guarantee mount-namespace immutability.
Directory identity checks narrow races; filesystem observations are not atomic. Inode reuse or changing file size can affect observed deduplication and sums.
Hardlink totals belong to the first observed path; enumeration order and group attribution are not stable. Partial caps may leave counters/groups/largest at different observation boundaries.
Cooperative elapsed budget cannot interrupt a blocked kernel call. Row/path/depth bounds are not a hard fixed JSON byte budget.

partial=False means no detected stop/error/qualifying skip within these observations; it does not certify whole-volume completeness, financial state, Railway volume identity, profitability, or restart safety.
No production metadata, financial contents, credentials, network policy or production service was accessed or changed by this review.
